fix(realtime): keep `None` disabling Voice Live turn detection; cover the semantic VAD path

Configure Azure AI Voice Live semantic VAD, end-of-utterance detection, noise suppression and echo cancellation Makes Azure AI Voice Live's own audio processing configurable: its semantic VAD, end-of-utterance detection, deep noise suppression and echo cancellation. Where an OpenAI setting doesn't fit a cascade model, it's adapted. The design was agreed with @DouweM before implementation. **Depends on #9407.** Without that harness fix, the new cassette trips `test_conformance`. I'll merge main in once it lands. **Settings** - **`azure_voice_live_turn_detection`** widens from `ServerVAD | SemanticVAD` to also take new public TypedDicts. The union only widens, so it's backward compatible. - `AzureServerVAD(ServerVAD)` adds `speech_duration_ms`, `auto_truncate` and `end_of_utterance_detection`. - `AzureSemanticVAD` covers `azure_semantic_vad` and `azure_semantic_vad_multilingual`, with `languages`, `remove_filler_words` and the rest. - `AzureEndOfUtteranceDetection` configures end-of-utterance detection. - Voice Live's shapes are sent as given, with the `create_response`/`interrupt_response` defaults filled in. `_openai_protocol.py` is untouched. - **`azure_voice_live_noise_reduction`**: `'azure_deep_noise_suppression' | 'near_field' | 'far_field'`. It overrides `openai_input_noise_reduction`. - **`azure_voice_live_echo_cancellation: bool`** sends `server_echo_cancellation`. **Adapting to the model** - **Noise reduction:** on a cascade model (`AzureRealtimeModelProfile.azure_voice_live_cascade`), `openai_input_noise_reduction` is sent as `azure_deep_noise_suppression`. Microsoft documents `near_field`/`far_field` as `gpt-realtime` only. - **End-of-utterance detection:** on a non-cascade model it raises `UserError` before connecting. Voice Live rejects it there and then refuses every later frame of the session. A cascade deployed under another name opts in with `profile=AzureRealtimeModelProfile(azure_voice_live_cascade=True)`. **Verified live on 2026-09-29** - On both native `gpt-realtime` and cascade `gpt-4.1`, Voice Live accepts all of these: - `azure_semantic_vad` and `azure_semantic_vad_multilingual` (with `languages` and `remove_filler_words`); - `azure_deep_noise_suppression`; - `server_echo_cancellation`; - `server_vad` with `speech_duration_ms` and `auto_truncate`. - End-of-utterance detection is accepted on cascade `gpt-4.1` and `phi4-mm-realtime`, and rejected on `gpt-realtime` and `azure-realtime` with "only supported on cascaded pipelines". - The new cassette records a spoken turn on `gpt-4.1` with multilingual Azure semantic VAD, end-of-utterance detection, `near_field` (sent as deep suppression) and echo cancellation. The server echoes each setting as applied. **Behavior change for existing users:** `openai_input_noise_reduction` on a cascade model now sends `azure_deep_noise_suppression`. That was approved. Nothing else changes for users who don't set the new options. **Docs:** a "Turn detection and audio processing" section with an example in `azure.md`, and the adaptation sentence now says exactly what's adapted. ### Checklist - [x] No **breaking changes** in accordance with the [version policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/version-policy.md). - [x] Any permitted **compatibility impact** has a label, warning, migration, release note, and exact API-check waiver. - [x] **PR title** is fit for the [release changelog](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

test(realtime): type the echo-cancellation test's settings

Checked live: Voice Live does not reject these on cascade models. `near_field` and `far_field` on `gpt-5` and `gpt-4.1` are accepted and echoed in `session.updated`; Microsoft only documents them as `gpt-realtime`-only. Converting is the absorb step for the shared OpenAI setting (`openai_input_noise_reduction`). `azure_voice_live_noise_reduction` is the explicit Voice Live setting, and per the approved design it is sent as given, which the test pins with a comment. Resolving.

**LOW:** the new guard only covers `azure_voice_live_turn_detection`, but the new public types are also assignable to the sibling settings.

`AzureServerVAD` is a `ServerVAD` subtype, so `openai_turn_detection=AzureServerVAD(type='server_vad', end_of_utterance_detection=...)` passes pyright against the inherited `openai_turn_detection: ServerVAD | SemanticVAD` field — yet such a value takes the `elif` at line 398 and falls through to `turn_detection_config` (line 412), which whitelists keys and silently strips `end_of_utterance_detection` (along with `speech_duration_ms`/`auto_truncate`). So on a cascade model where EOU would work, the session silently opens without it — the exact misconfiguration this guard raises loudly for when it comes through the documented setting.

Consider moving the `'end_of_utterance_detection' in turn_detection and not cascade` check below the setting-resolution chain so it also covers `openai_turn_detection`/`turn_detection`, or noting in the `azure_voice_live_turn_detection` docstring that the Azure-only VAD options are honored only through that setting.

fix(realtime): honor Azure-only VAD options and the end-of-utterance guard from `openai_turn_detection` too

Fixed: the end-of-utterance guard and the pass-through of Azure-only options now run after the setting is resolved, so they apply equally to `openai_turn_detection` (and the shared `turn_detection`). An `AzureServerVAD` passed there keeps `end_of_utterance_detection`, `speech_duration_ms` and `auto_truncate` on a cascade, and is rejected early on a native model. Tests cover both.
